summary: Blind-scored case-1: 3 RT findings, 16 CX and 16 CY (X/Y sources identical). PRESENT: RT-3 only in X; CX-9/11/15 in X; CY-9/11/15 in Y. All PRESENT marks DISPOSED. GT-1 CONSISTENT in X (4/13 = 30.8%) and CONTRADICTS in Y (rate believed zero).

rt.statement: Keeping Proposal A (the flat OR-chain) ignores internal maintainability and producer-side scaling by leaning on consumer output shape.
rt.quote: ignores internal maintainability/producer-side scaling by leaning on consumer output shape.

rt.statement: looksStructured is a dumping ground of hardcoded, tool-specific heuristics; as CLI producers grow, the flat OR-chain will balloon into an unmaintainable, brittle regex nightmare / accumulating technical debt.
rt.quote: The `looksStructured` function is a dumping ground of hardcoded, highly specific heuristics targeting exact tools. [...] As the number of supported CLI tools (producers) grows, this flat OR-chain will inevitably balloon into an unmaintainable, brittle regex nightmare.

rt.statement: Missing legitimate hybrid: array of modular independently-testable predicate functions (Strategy pattern; Classifier = (lines: string[]) => boolean; HEURISTICS.some), solving producer-side maintainability without a grammar registry.
rt.quote: A simple, legitimate hybrid would be to extract the heuristics into an array of modular predicate functions (the Strategy pattern) conforming to a simple interface, e.g., `type Classifier = (lines: string[]) => boolean`.
rt.X_quote: An array of modular predicate functions — a Strategy-pattern refactor. Same behaviour, same OR-composition, same file if you like; each detector extracted into its own named unit and the chain becomes an iteration over them.

cx.statement: Proposal A conflates consumer output shape with implementation architecture.
Flat OR-chain in one file will degrade block-classify.ts into a God Function.
OCP: every new CLI layout requires modifying core looksStructured / a sensitive path.
Regression risk: new heuristics in a flat OR-chain can catch prose; no isolation.
Cognitive overload from mixed domains as the heuristic list grows.
Internal composition must be modular to absorb CLI-format churn; a flat OR-chain fails that.
Registry adds no value to the caller because terminal-render.ts only consumes binary block.mode.
No demonstrated Phase 5 need for runtime-pluggable detectors; registry is YAGNI.
Six checks are empirically patched special cases; independently-registered units risk losing interaction context.
cx.X_quote: One constant is narrowed so a different detector can claim what it gave up. Today those two notes sit forty lines apart and a reader hits both. Under B they live in a box-drawing grammar module and a q-and-a-summary grammar module respectively.

cx.statement: Wrongly-panned structured block is unrecoverable; wrongly-wrapped prose matches old behavior.
Debuggability of top-to-bottom classification is a safety property; dynamic registration is harder to trace than a linear if-chain.
cx.X_quote: B is behaviourally identical to A and pays for that identity with a specific, concrete loss of debuggability.

cx.statement: Configurable registration order/active detectors risks breaking the text-only verdict invariant.
B has full rewrite/migration cost against 6 heuristics with no shown correctness or extensibility win.
Forward risk of A: independent ORs may quietly become order-dependent as detectors accumulate.
A and C are not independent designs; they produce the same already-shipping code; real fork is B vs not-B.
cx.X_quote: Proposal C — the status quo, which is Proposal A. Same shape, different label.

cx.statement: Unresolved whether a concrete Phase 5 requirement drives B or B is speculative.
